La palabra <em>compilador</em> es de <st: The word compiler is Grace Hopper's, and originally it meant something rather different from what it means today: her A-0 of 1952 compiled in the sense of collecting, joining pieces of already written code held on a tape. She had trouble convincing anybody: the usual reply was that computers only knew how to do arithmetic and that translating words was a matter for people. The first compiler in the modern sense was FORTRAN's, and its declared aim was that the generated code should be as good as what a competent programmer would write by hand, because otherwise nobody would use it. They managed it, and that is why hardly anybody writes assembly today.
La única forma de saberlo es correr el p: The only way of knowing is to run the program by both routes and compare what they print. This course does it: there is a battery of eleven programs, with loops, functions, recursion and mutual recursion, which on each run of the tests are interpreted and compiled and executed on the machine, and the two outputs are compared. That is called a differential test, and it is no ornament: the first version of this compiler passed inspection perfectly and got suma(1, suma(2, 3)) wrong when compiling. This test caught it with a three-line program.
